newsitem.title: USA: Netanyahu says no preconditions to Washington talks.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says no preconditions to Washington talks.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday he was coming to Washington for Mideast talks this week with President Bill Clinton and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat without preconditions.
Asked about any preconditions on the ABC-TV's "This Week" programme, he said "in fact, that was my only precondition, that we all come without preconditions."

Netanyahu said "I would like, as I said to Arafat, and he knew fully well, to engage on all the outstanding issues of negotiations. I think though that we have to understand that we face some of the most difficult negotiations in the history of nations."

Asked if he would keep open a disputed tunnel near Jerusalem's al-Aqsa Mosque, Islam's third holiest site, which touched off violence, Netanyahu said "I think it's not an issue. For me the crucial issue is how to we engage the peace process."
That, he said, would start with an end to the violence.

Netanyahu added that the violence over the tunnel did not begin until 24 hours after it was opened and that "we have clear indications that the Palestinian authority used a fabricated description of what this tunnel is about to spark off organised demonstrations."
